newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call rates, securities end nearly unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Indian call rates, securities end nearly unchanged.

text.p: Indian call money closed at 10.60-75 percent on Tuesday, compared to the day's opening of 10.50-10.80 percent, dealers said.
A dealer at Discount and Finance House of India (DHFI) said the day opened at 10.80, lenders were quoting 10.75 and above, but most of the deals were in the 10.50-75 percent levels.
"There was demand for treasury bills maturing in October 1996 and September 1997," she said.

Market was very dull and dealers were quoting two way prices for government securities with one paise or one basis point difference, a dealer at National Stock Exchange said. But there was hardly any demand, he added.

Gilt prices were steady today with 13.62 percent maturing in 1998 traded at 13.46, 13.50 percent maturing 1998 traded at 13.39 percent and 13.82 percent maturing in 2002 traded at 13.85 percent, a dealer said.
He said treasury bills maturing in November 1996 were traded at 10.30 percent and September 1997 at 12.80 percent.

Market saw little activity in commercial paper (CP) and commercial deposits (CD). ICICI CDs maturing in February were traded at 14.10 percent, a dealer said. The intercorporate deposit were steady at 17-19 percent for blue-chip companies, he added.
